items.title: Around 90% of LIC employment is informal
items.claim: What share of work is informal in low-income countries?

options.text: Around 90% of employment in LICs and around 60% globally is informal (ILO 2018) — work without legal recognition, social protection or tax registration, totalling around 2 billion workers worldwide

items.reveal:
The International Labour Organization defines informal employment as work without legal recognition or social protection. Concentrations are high in sub-Saharan Africa (around 89% of non-agricultural employment) and South Asia (around 86%).

Main activities: street vending, waste-picking, small-scale agriculture, domestic work, informal manufacturing. Many informal workers are women; many have no fixed workplace.

Keith Hart's 1971 Accra fieldwork coined the modern use of 'informal sector'. ILO Recommendation 204 (2015) framed transition strategies to formal employment.
items.why: Models built on Global North wage labour misrepresent developing economies. The informal sector is not marginal — it is the modal experience of work for two billion people.

items.title: The jet stream sits around 10 km up at the tropopause

options.text: A narrow band of fast westerly winds (typically 100-300 km/h) at around 9-12 km altitude, near the tropopause, driven by temperature contrasts between polar and tropical air masses
An ocean current in the Pacific
A jet of supersonic air over deserts

items.reveal:
The polar jet (which shapes UK weather) and the subtropical jet are the major Northern Hemisphere features. They meander in Rossby waves; the shape of those waves controls where storm tracks lie.

Jet streams were discovered by Japanese balloon-bombing campaigns of WWII and by US B-29 crews over the Pacific (1944) — flying west into apparently impossible headwinds. Carl-Gustaf Rossby's work in the 1930s-40s framed them theoretically.

Arctic amplification reduces the temperature contrast that drives the polar jet, possibly causing it to meander more — linked to more persistent weather extremes (heat domes, stuck storm tracks).
items.why: Surface weather has upper-atmosphere causes. Understanding why summer 2022 had heat domes or why winter 2013-14 had stuck Atlantic storm tracks requires looking at jet stream geometry.

items.title: OS contour lines show points of equal elevation
items.claim: What do OS contour lines show?

options.text: Lines connecting points of equal elevation above sea level — close contours indicate steep slopes; OS 1:50,000 Landranger maps typically use 10 m intervals; 1:25,000 Explorer maps use 5 or 10 m intervals depending on relief

items.reveal:
Closed loop contours with highest values inside indicate a hill summit. V-shaped contours pointing uphill indicate river valleys (water flows perpendicular to contours, downhill). Cliffs are shown by hachures or special vertical symbols.

Index contours (heavier lines) are labelled — typically every 50 m on 1:50,000 maps. Spot heights and trig points (triangulation pillars) give precise local elevations.

OS symbol conventions: black for human features, blue for water, brown for relief, green for vegetation, purple for tourist information. Knowing the key is half the skill.
items.why: Map literacy is portable across navigation, fieldwork and planning. Visual grammar (contour interval, symbol conventions) underpins all higher-level interpretation.
